correctness.rationale: For nonnegative Fourier frequencies summing N=3M, the bijection (M+x,M+y,M-x-y) converts the Laplacian eigenvalue to 3M²+2(x²+xy+y²). Classical unique factorization of Z[omega] gives r_Q(m)=6 sum_{d|m} chi_{-3}(d). A forbidden nonnegative-frequency triple first occurs at Q=ceil(3(M+1)^2/4): any negative coordinate is <=-M-1, completed square gives lower bound, and nearest y to (M+1)/2 attains it with x=-M-1. Thus the arithmetic band is exact and first excluded value genuinely loses representations. For every N, the uniform frequency lattice on a triangle gives the circular-cap CDF for sum t_i²; bounded convex perimeter yields a uniform CDF O(1/N) discretization error; differentiation gives square-root cusp coefficient 6 sqrt(2) at 1/2. Zero center and N not divisible by three treated separately; no unrestricted divisor rule beyond the sharp cutoff is asserted.

evidence: General Eisenstein representation identity already implies unrestricted r_Q(m) and generic convex lattice-discrepancy O(N^-1) independently; neither supplies the sharp first lost representation threshold as a combined spectral statement.
